chunks: Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūn informed me, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn al-Zubayr, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAlī ibn Asbāṭ, from ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two of them, peace be upon them, who said:

I said: A woman sees that she has become pure at the time of al-ẓuhr, but she busies herself with her affairs until the time of al-ʿaṣr enters. He said: She should perform al-ʿaṣr alone; but if she neglected it, then two salats (prayers) are upon her.

key_terms.الطُّهْرَ: cessation of menstruation and attainment of ritual purity
key_terms.ضَيَّعَتْ: she neglected or let it lapse
key_terms.وَحْدَهَا: by itself, meaning only that prayer alone
key_terms.وَقْتُ الْعَصْرِ: the time of the afternoon prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a menstruating woman becomes pure at al-ẓuhr but delays until the time of al-ʿaṣr?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about a menstruating woman who becomes pure around the time of al-ẓuhr but delays until the time of al-ʿaṣr begins. It indicates that if the earlier time was missed due to delay, she performs al-ʿaṣr, and if she further neglects that obligation, then both prayers become due upon her.
